# EmitMovie <img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [3D Sound](Blitz3D-3D-Sound)

</div>


```blitzbasic
EmitMovie:Void movie:Int32, entity:Int32
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `movie` | In | Int32 | required | A movie handle from [OpenMovie](OpenMovie). |
| `entity` | In | Int32 | required | The entity that the sound comes from, or `0` to play it on the speakers again. |

## Description

<img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14"> This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

Makes the sound of a movie come from an entity in the world, like [EmitSound](EmitSound): it gets quieter with distance and moves between the speakers. With [GetMovieTexture](GetMovieTexture) on a mesh this makes a screen in the world. This is a BlitzLLVM extension.

## Differences

* The sound of a movie gets no doppler shift: a change of pitch would play it faster or slower than the picture. [ChannelDoppler](ChannelDoppler) on it is ignored. A movie without sound, or without a sound device, ignores the command.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Graphics3D 640, 480, 0, 2
camera = CreateCamera()
CreateListener camera
movie  = OpenMovie("advert.mp4")
LoopMovie movie
screen = CreateCube()
PositionEntity screen, 0, 0, 10
ScaleEntity screen, 4, 2.25, 0.1
EntityTexture screen, GetMovieTexture(movie)
EmitMovie movie, screen
ChannelRadius MovieChannel(movie), 2 ; the screen is 4 units wide
```
